stated in less technical language.
On page 90 you quote an E.P.A. prediction, "... as newer automobiles, equipped with emission control devices, replace the older vehicles carbon monoxide emissions will...". You fail to identify the source of the quote. What is the source of this quote—the EPA publication and page number?<sup>2.</sup>
On page 91 you state, "Since these models will be equipped with exhaust emission controls, emission factors should be constant and relatively independent of route speed." (emphasis added). Yet in the accompanying table you list the route speed as a factor in terms of the differences in route speed between freeways and local streets. Isn't this a contradiction? If it is an explanation is in order. 3.
II. THE AIRPORT SPUR IN CONFLICT WITH THE NATIONAL, STATE, AND DEPARTMENTAL GOALS.
It is very clear that in the last two years, public officials in all ranks of government, governmental agencies, and citizens have changed their outlook on transportation goals. Increasing concern about the decreasing reserves of petroleum and dwindling land resources have prompted the revamping and reappraisal of these goals. We can see this change demonstrated on the national level in the Report of the Office of Emergency Preparedness, Executive Office of the President, entitled, "The Potential For Energy Conservation"; on the state level in the recent pronouncements of Governor Lucey and Attorney General Warren; in the Wisconsin Department of Transportation in a document entitled, Transportation Planning Objectives, Principles and Standards.
On the national level such a change in attitudes is demonstrated in the energy conservation report,
"Given present concern over the environment, fuel resources, and increasing U.S. dependence on foreign petroleum, optimistic plans for quantum jumps in air transportation and increasing dependence on automobiles in urban areas... seem questionable" (pg. 14)
and in a later statement in appendix C-ll it speaks directly to the issue at and, "Current government policy is function ing in at least two basic ways to aggravate the energy problem. First it favors development of air and highway transport..."
